request.subject: The Dog Who Never Stopped Waiting - part 2: Waiting at Shibuya Station
request.title: The Dog Who Never Stopped Waiting (Part 2/3)
request.description:
Hachiko kept going back to Shibuya Station long after his owner died, until a newspaper made him a national hero. Could you wait that long?

Part 2 of 3: The Dog Who Never Stopped Waiting

Sources:
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hachik%C5%8D
https://www.nippon.com/en/japan-glances/jg00137/
https://www.gotokyo.org/en/spot/86/index.html

Stock footage: Pexels. Made with AI-assisted narration.

#shorts #truestory

extra_params.video_script: Hachiko went back to the station every single day. In Part 1, his owner, Professor Ueno, died suddenly at work in 1925. Hachiko was passed between caretakers, but he kept returning to Shibuya Station, waiting for a train that never brought Ueno home. Some people kicked him and pushed him away. Then, in 1932, a newspaper told his story, and all of Japan fell in love with him. People brought him food. Teachers called him a lesson in loyalty. But in 1934, Hachiko got something most heroes only get after they die. Subscribe so you don't miss Part 3.
